passages.heading: It's Time to Trust Americans Again.
passages.text: Freedom isn't Left or Right. It's American.

passages.heading: It's Time to Trust Americans Again.
passages.text: Washington has forgotten who it's supposed to serve. I believe government should trust Americans more than Washington trusts itself. Together, we can restore constitutional government, protect individual liberty, and return power where it belongs—with the people.

passages.heading: It's Time to Trust Americans Again.
passages.text: Navy Veteran • Father • Public Servant • Constitutional Libertarian

passages.heading: Why I'm Running
passages.text: For twenty years, I had the privilege of serving our nation in the United States Navy. After retiring, I chose a different kind of service—raising my children, giving back to my community, and continuing to learn and grow as a husband, father, and citizen.

passages.heading: Why I'm Running
passages.text: I never planned to run for Congress. Like many Americans, I believed that if I worked hard, raised my family, and did my part, I could make a difference where I lived. But over time, I watched Washington become more focused on growing its own power than serving the people who entrusted it with that responsibility.

passages.heading: Why I'm Running
passages.text: That's why I'm running. I believe government should trust Americans more than Washington trusts itself. I believe the Constitution still matters, individual liberty is worth protecting, and public office is an opportunity to serve—not to rule.

passages.heading: Why I'm Running
passages.text: I’m not running to become a career politician. I’m running to be your representative.

passages.heading: There Is Another Way.
passages.text: For too long, Americans have been told they have only two choices: bigger government from one party or bigger government from the other. I don't believe that's the future our Founders envisioned, and I don't believe it's the future the American people deserve.

passages.heading: There Is Another Way.
passages.text: There is another way—one that trusts the people, respects the Constitution, protects individual liberty, and expects government to live within the limits placed on it by the people it serves.

passages.heading: There Is Another Way.
passages.text: This campaign isn't about left versus right. It's about restoring the principles that made America strong: personal responsibility, equal justice under the law, fiscal responsibility, and the freedom to build your own future.

passages.heading: There Is Another Way.
passages.text: "Freedom isn't Left or Right. It's American."

passages.heading: There Is Another Way.
passages.text: Government exists because of the people. It answers to the people. And it should always serve the people.

passages.heading: There Is Another Way.
passages.text: That principle shaped our founding documents. It should still guide our government today.

passages.heading: Your Money
passages.text: Lower taxes. Responsible spending. End government waste.

passages.heading: Your Freedom
passages.text: Defend the Constitution. Protect individual liberty. Limit federal overreach.

passages.heading: Your Vote
passages.text: Honest representation. Transparent government. Every voice matters.

passages.heading: Meet Brian
passages.text: I am a Navy veteran, a father, and a citizen who believes public office should be about service—not power.

passages.heading: 20 Years in the U.S. Navy
passages.text: Twenty years of service taught me leadership, discipline, accountability, and the importance of putting the mission before personal ambition.

passages.heading: Father of Three
passages.text: Raising my children has made the future of this country personal. Our children deserve more freedom, greater opportunity, and a government that lives within its means.

passages.heading: Constitution First
passages.text: The Constitution limits the government, not the citizen. Every vote I cast will begin with one question: Is this constitutional?

passages.heading: Citizen Legislator
passages.text: Congress should be filled with citizens who serve for a time—not politicians who build lifelong careers in Washington. I will serve, remain accountable, and come home.

passages.heading: Highlighted Issues
passages.text: Campaign promises should be clear before Election Day. Here are some of the issues that matter most to me and the people of our district.

passages.heading: Fiscal Responsibility
passages.text: Washington does not have a revenue problem—it has a spending problem. I will fight for balanced budgets, honest accounting, and an end to reckless spending that leaves our children with the bill.

passages.heading: Constitutional Government
passages.text: Government must operate within its constitutional limits, remain transparent, and answer to the people it serves.

passages.heading: Veterans
passages.text: Veterans earned their benefits through service and sacrifice. I will fight for greater choice, less bureaucracy, real accountability, and care that puts the veteran first.

passages.heading: Fiscal Responsibility
passages.text: Washington doesn't have a revenue problem—it has a spending problem. Every dollar the federal government wastes is a dollar taken from hardworking Americans or borrowed from future generations.

passages.heading: America's Greatest National Security Threat
passages.text: America's national debt has become the single greatest long-term threat to our national security. A nation buried beneath trillions of dollars in debt cannot remain economically strong, strategically independent, or leave future generations the country they deserve.

passages.heading: America's Greatest National Security Threat
passages.text: Every dollar Washington borrows today is a bill sent to our children tomorrow. We cannot continue spending money we do not have while expecting future Americans to bear the burden.

passages.heading: America's Greatest National Security Threat
passages.text: Fiscal responsibility is not simply about balancing numbers on a ledger. It is about preserving America's independence, protecting our economic future, and honoring our obligation to leave the next generation a stronger nation than the one we inherited.

passages.heading: Why This Matters
passages.text: The national debt continues to grow while Congress spends money it doesn't have. Inflation has quietly reduced the purchasing power of every American family.

passages.heading: Why This Matters
passages.text: Government should live within its means just like the people it represents. Families balance budgets every day. Washington should be expected to do the same.

passages.heading: Pass a Balanced Budget
passages.text: Congress should be required to live within its means just as American families do.

passages.heading: Confront the National Debt
passages.text: America's national debt has become the single greatest long-term threat to our national security and the future prosperity of our children.

passages.heading: End Reckless Spending
passages.text: Washington must stop spending money it doesn't have and adding to the national debt.

passages.heading: Stop Inflationary Money Printing
passages.text: Printing trillions of dollars devalues every paycheck and every retirement account.

passages.heading: Audit Federal Agencies
passages.text: Every federal agency should be accountable for how it spends taxpayer dollars.

passages.heading: Eliminate Unconstitutional Bureaucracies
passages.text: Agencies that exceed the powers granted by the Constitution should be reduced or eliminated.

passages.heading: Hold Congress Accountable
passages.text: Members of Congress should be held responsible for the nation's fiscal health, not rewarded for reckless spending.

passages.heading: Protect Future Generations
passages.text: Restore fiscal responsibility so our children inherit opportunity instead of crushing debt.

passages.heading: The Bottom Line
passages.text: Fiscal responsibility isn't just about balancing numbers on a spreadsheet. It's about honoring the trust taxpayers place in their government. Every dollar Washington spends was earned by someone who worked for it.

passages.heading: The Bottom Line
passages.text: We can restore accountability, reduce waste, and build a government that lives within its means. That's how we protect both our economy and the future of our children.

passages.heading: Government Accountability
passages.text: Congress and federal agencies must answer to the Constitution and the people they serve.

passages.heading: Energy Independence
passages.text: Affordable, reliable American energy strengthens families, businesses, and national security.

passages.heading: Individual Liberty
passages.text: Your earnings, choices, and future should not be controlled by an oversized federal government.

passages.text: Learn how twenty years of Navy service, fatherhood, and community involvement shaped Brian’s commitment to public service.

passages.text: Explore Brian’s positions on the issues affecting families, veterans, businesses, and communities across Florida’s 14th District.

passages.heading: Veterans
passages.text: My service didn't end with retirement. It simply gave me a new way to serve.

passages.heading: Why This Matters
passages.text: For twenty years, I wore the uniform of the United States Navy. Retirement didn't end my commitment to serving others—it simply gave me a new way to serve.

passages.heading: Why This Matters
passages.text: Our nation has a solemn obligation to every man and woman who answered the call to defend it. That obligation doesn't end when they take off the uniform.

passages.heading: Why This Matters
passages.text: Keeping our promises to veterans means more than speeches on Veterans Day. It means ensuring we receive the care, respect, and support we've earned through our service.

passages.heading: Why This Matters
passages.text: Veteran suicide isn't just another policy issue to me. Over the years, I’ve received the devastating news that thirteen friends and members of my squadron—people I flew with and turned wrenches beside—lost the battle within.

passages.heading: Why This Matters
passages.text: Those losses are something I carry with me. They remind me that when we ask Americans to wear the uniform, our responsibility to them doesn't end when they take it off. That's why this isn't just another campaign promise for me. It's personal.

passages.heading: My Perspective
passages.text: My experience with the Department of Veterans Affairs has generally been a positive one. I've been fortunate to receive quality care from doctors, nurses, and staff who truly care about veterans.

passages.heading: My Perspective
passages.text: Where I believe we need improvement isn't with the people—it's with the bureaucracy.

passages.heading: My Perspective
passages.text: Too many veterans spend months waiting on claims, navigating unnecessary paperwork, or struggling to access the care they've already earned. We can do better, and we owe it to every man and woman who served.

passages.heading: Protect Earned Benefits
passages.text: Benefits earned through military service should never be treated as political bargaining chips.

passages.heading: Cut VA Bureaucracy
passages.text: Veterans should not have to fight months of paperwork to receive the care and benefits they have earned.

passages.heading: Improve VA Accountability
passages.text: The Department of Veterans Affairs must serve veterans first, not protect broken systems.

passages.heading: Expand Community Care
passages.text: When the VA cannot provide timely treatment, veterans should have access to care in their own communities.

passages.heading: Strengthen Mental Health Support
passages.text: PTSD, suicide prevention, and mental health treatment must be treated with urgency and seriousness.

passages.heading: Respect Veteran Choice
passages.text: Veterans should have access to traditional medicine, community care, mental health support, and complementary, holistic, herbal, and alternative therapies when appropriate in consultation with their healthcare providers.

passages.heading: The Bottom Line
passages.text: No veteran who survived the battlefield should come home and lose the battle within. Every veteran suicide is a tragedy, and one is too many.

passages.heading: The Bottom Line
passages.text: We owe our veterans more than gratitude—we owe them a system that responds quickly, treats them with dignity, and never stops working to ensure every veteran has hope, support, and access to the care they've earned.

passages.heading: The Bottom Line
passages.text: Until veteran suicide is no longer a daily reality, our work is not finished.

passages.heading: My Oath
passages.text: For twenty years, I swore an oath to support and defend the Constitution of the United States against all enemies, foreign and domestic.

passages.heading: My Oath
passages.text: That oath did not end the day I retired from the United States Navy. It is a promise that continues to guide my life and my service.

passages.heading: My Oath
passages.text: Before I cast a vote, I'll ask one question: Is it constitutional?

passages.heading: National Defense
passages.text: A strong national defense requires responsible leadership and an enduring commitment to those who serve.

passages.heading: Healthcare Reform
passages.text: Veterans and their families deserve timely care, real choices, and a healthcare system focused on patients.

passages.heading: Government Accountability
passages.text: Federal agencies, including the VA, must answer for delays, failures, and the treatment of those they serve.

passages.heading: Every Legal Vote. Counted Fairly.
passages.text: Election Integrity • Transparency • Public Confidence

passages.heading: Why It Matters
passages.text: Confidence in our elections is essential to preserving our republic. Regardless of political party, every American should trust that elections are conducted fairly, transparently, and according to the law.

passages.heading: Why It Matters
passages.text: Election integrity is not about helping one party or hurting another. It is about ensuring that every eligible citizen has the opportunity to vote, every legal vote is counted accurately, and every election is conducted with transparency and accountability.

passages.heading: Why It Matters
passages.text: Public trust is earned through consistent rules, secure procedures, and open oversight—not political rhetoric.

passages.heading: Where I Stand
passages.text: I support election systems that are secure, transparent, and easy for eligible citizens to use while making fraud difficult to commit and easy to detect.

passages.heading: Where I Stand
passages.text: States should continue leading election administration while Congress respects constitutional limits on federal authority.

passages.heading: Where I Stand
passages.text: Every lawful voter deserves confidence that their vote carries the same weight as every other lawful vote.

passages.heading: Where I Stand
passages.text: Americans should never have to question whether the rules were applied fairly to everyone.

passages.heading: Protect Every Legal Vote
passages.text: Every eligible citizen should be able to vote, and every legal vote should be counted accurately.

passages.heading: Promote Transparency
passages.text: Election processes should be open, observable, and accountable to the public.

passages.heading: Support Secure Elections
passages.text: Election systems should protect against fraud while remaining accessible to lawful voters.

passages.heading: Respect Constitutional Authority
passages.text: Election administration should remain consistent with the Constitution and the role of the states.

passages.heading: Ensure Equal Application of the Law
passages.text: Election laws should be applied fairly and consistently to every voter, every campaign, and every jurisdiction.

passages.heading: Restore Public Confidence
passages.text: Confidence in elections strengthens confidence in our entire constitutional republic.

passages.heading: Bottom Line
passages.text: Our elections should leave Americans with confidence—not doubt. Every eligible citizen deserves the opportunity to vote, and every legal vote deserves to be counted fairly, accurately, and transparently.

passages.heading: Bottom Line
passages.text: Public confidence in our elections strengthens confidence in our republic itself.

passages.heading: Government Accountability
passages.text: Transparent government and meaningful oversight are essential to maintaining public trust.

passages.heading: Individual Liberty
passages.text: Every eligible citizen deserves a secure vote and confidence that their voice will be heard.

passages.heading: Fiscal Responsibility
passages.text: Election systems should protect public trust while using taxpayer resources responsibly.

passages.heading: Constitutional Government
passages.text: The Constitution limits the government—not the people.

passages.heading: Why It Matters
passages.text: The Constitution was not written to control the American people. It was written to limit the power of the federal government and protect the liberty of the people.

passages.heading: Why It Matters
passages.text: When Washington expands beyond its constitutional limits, government becomes less accountable, less transparent, and farther removed from the people it serves.

passages.heading: Where I Stand
passages.text: I believe every bill should begin with one question: does the Constitution authorize the federal government to do this?

passages.heading: Where I Stand
passages.text: Congress must respect the separation of powers, protect the Bill of Rights, review the scope of federal agencies, and return appropriate authority closer to the people and the states.

passages.heading: Begin with the Constitution
passages.text: Every vote I take will begin with whether the Constitution authorizes the federal government to act.

passages.heading: Defend the Bill of Rights
passages.text: The rights of the people are not privileges granted by Washington.

passages.heading: Respect Separation of Powers
passages.text: No branch of government should be allowed to exceed its constitutional role.

passages.heading: Limit Federal Overreach
passages.text: Federal agencies should not exercise powers never granted by the Constitution.

passages.heading: Return Power to the People
passages.text: Government should remain closest to the people whenever possible.

passages.heading: Choose Principle Over Politics
passages.text: My oath is to the Constitution, not to party leaders or political pressure.

passages.heading: Bottom Line
passages.text: The Constitution does not limit freedom. It protects freedom by limiting government.

passages.heading: Bottom Line
passages.text: My responsibility is to the Constitution and to the people of Florida's 14th Congressional District. If political pressure ever conflicts with either, I will choose principle over politics.

passages.heading: Individual Liberty
passages.text: Every American is born with rights. Government does not create those rights, and it should not take them away.

passages.heading: Why This Matters
passages.text: Liberty is not a gift from government. It is the birthright of every American.

passages.heading: Why This Matters
passages.text: Free speech, privacy, property rights, due process, religious liberty, and the right to keep and bear arms are not optional. They are protected by the Constitution and must be defended without apology.

passages.heading: Why This Matters
passages.text: When government treats freedom like a permission slip, it stops serving the people and starts ruling over them.

passages.heading: Defend the Bill of Rights
passages.text: The Bill of Rights is not a list of government privileges. It is a boundary government must not cross.

passages.heading: Protect Free Speech
passages.text: Americans should never fear government punishment for speaking their minds or challenging those in power.

passages.heading: Protect Religious Liberty
passages.text: Government has no authority to dictate matters of conscience, faith, or belief.

passages.heading: Defend the Second Amendment
passages.text: The right to keep and bear arms is a constitutional right and must be protected.

passages.heading: Protect Privacy and Property
passages.text: Americans have the right to be secure in their homes, property, personal data, and private lives.

passages.heading: Oppose Government Overreach
passages.text: Personal decisions should remain with individuals and families, not federal bureaucrats.

passages.heading: The Bottom Line
passages.text: Liberty is not negotiable. It does not belong to the government, and it should never depend on which party is in power.

passages.heading: The Bottom Line
passages.text: Freedom is not Left or Right. It is American.

passages.heading: Government Accountability
passages.text: Government must remain within its constitutional limits and answer to the people it serves.

passages.heading: Second Amendment
passages.text: The right to keep and bear arms is an individual liberty that government must not infringe.

passages.heading: Healthcare Reform
passages.text: Patients should control their healthcare decisions without unnecessary government interference.

passages.heading: Your Money. Your Freedom. Your Vote.
passages.text: Every issue deserves more than a campaign slogan. Here's exactly where I stand.

passages.heading: Fiscal Responsibility
passages.text: Restore fiscal discipline, balance the budget, and protect future generations from crushing debt.

passages.heading: Constitutional Government
passages.text: The Constitution limits the government—not the people. Every law begins there.

passages.heading: Individual Liberty
passages.text: Protect the freedoms guaranteed by the Bill of Rights and defend individual choice.

passages.heading: Second Amendment
passages.text: Protect the right to keep and bear arms and defend the Constitution without compromise.

passages.heading: Veterans
passages.text: America must keep its promises to the men and women who served.

passages.heading: Border Security & Immigration
passages.text: Secure every border and port of entry while supporting legal immigration and the rule of law.

passages.heading: Healthcare Reform
passages.text: Restore patient choice, medical freedom, price transparency, and competition while reducing unnecessary federal interference in healthcare.

passages.heading: Education
passages.text: Education is not one-size-fits-all. Empower parents, support teachers, and give every child the opportunity to succeed.

passages.heading: National Defense
passages.text: Peace through strength, constitutional accountability, and unwavering support for our troops.

passages.heading: Economy & Small Business
passages.text: Lower taxes, reduce regulation, and let American entrepreneurs succeed.

passages.heading: Election Integrity
passages.text: Restore confidence through transparency, accountability, and secure elections.

passages.heading: Energy & American Independence
passages.text: Reliable, affordable energy strengthens our economy, protects national security, and reduces dependence on foreign adversaries.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: I didn't become a Libertarian because it was politically convenient.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: I became a Libertarian because I reached a point where I could no longer ignore what I was seeing.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: For twenty years, I served this country in the United States Navy. I swore an oath to support and defend the Constitution of the United States—not a political party, not a president, and not a government bureaucracy.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: Like millions of Americans, I've watched Washington spend money it doesn't have, pass laws it was never meant to pass, and grow further away from the people it is supposed to serve. Election after election, we're told that this time will be different.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: At some point, I stopped asking which party was responsible and started asking a different question:

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: The Constitution was written to limit the power of government, not the freedom of the people. Somewhere along the way, we've allowed that relationship to be turned upside down. Today, too many politicians act as though our rights come from Washington, when in reality they exist long before any government does.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: I don't believe freedom belongs to Republicans.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: I don't believe freedom belongs to Democrats.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: To me, being Libertarian isn't about winning arguments or fitting into a political label. It's about believing that free people are better at running their own lives than politicians are.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: I trust parents to raise their children.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: I trust workers to earn their own success.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: I trust entrepreneurs to build opportunity.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: And I trust the American people far more than I trust Washington.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: That doesn't mean government has no role.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: Government has an important responsibility: to defend our nation, protect our constitutional rights, uphold the rule of law, and perform the limited duties assigned to it by the Constitution.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: But when government reaches beyond those limits, liberty always pays the price.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: That's why I believe Congress should balance the budget instead of passing debt to our children.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: That's why I believe inflation is a hidden tax created by reckless spending.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: That's why I believe every bill should first answer one simple question:

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: If the answer is no, it shouldn't become law.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: My campaign isn't about expanding government in a different direction.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: It's about returning government to its proper size, its proper role, and its proper limits.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: One of the greatest strengths of America is that we're free to disagree.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: But I hope we can all agree on one thing:

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: Government exists because of the people.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: I didn't choose the Libertarian Party because I was looking for a team.

passages.heading: Why I Believe
passages.text: I chose it because its principles most closely match the oath I took years ago and the country I still believe in today.

passages.heading: A Life of Service
passages.text: For twenty years, I proudly served our nation in the United States Navy. During that time I served as an Aircraft Mechanic (AM), a Flight Engineer (AWF), and an Intelligence Specialist (IS). Each role carried different responsibilities, but they all demanded discipline, integrity, and a commitment to serving something greater than myself.

passages.heading: A Life of Service
passages.text: While serving in the Navy, I became a Motorcycle Safety Foundation RiderCoach, helping new riders develop the skills and confidence to ride safely. I continued coaching for a short time after retiring from military service in 2018.

passages.heading: A Life of Service
passages.text: After retirement, I chose to dedicate my time to raising my children and giving back to my community. I coached Little League baseball, studied culinary arts at the Art Institute of Tampa, and continue pursuing new knowledge as I work toward an Associate of Science in Firearms Technology through Sonoran Desert Institute.

passages.heading: A Life of Service
passages.text: Today I'm running for Congress because I believe government exists to serve the American people—not the other way around. My goal isn't to grow government. My goal is to restore constitutional government, protect individual liberty, and return power to the people.

passages.heading: A Life of Service
passages.text: The Constitution wasn't written because Americans couldn't be trusted. It was written because government couldn't.
